name: International Trade Breakdown
description: A major geopolitical dispute has triggered closure of the Strait of Hormuz to commercial traffic. Your company depends on this route for 60% of raw material imports. Port capacity has collapsed and shipping costs are spiking. Manage a cascading maritime logistics crisis through five decision rounds, balancing inventory survival against cash preservation and long-term supply chain resilience.

actors.name: Strait Port Authority
actors.description: Controls access to the affected strait. Unresponsive to commercial pressure; responds only to diplomatic channels.

actors.name: Global Shipping Consortium
actors.description: Controls 80% of available alternate-route vessels. Expensive but reliable when engaged early.

actors.name: Government Relations Office
actors.description: Can pursue diplomatic resolution but requires 2–3 rounds of negotiation. Reduces geopolitical_risk_level by 1 per engagement.

actors.name: Marine Insurance Underwriter
actors.description: Standard coverage excludes geopolitical closures. Enhanced coverage available at cost but covers rerouting premiums.

actors.name: Secondary Regional Supplier
actors.description: 15% lower quality but geographically unconstrained. Can be activated within 1 round at a one-time cost.

actors.name: Internal Financial Controller
actors.description: Monitors cash reserves and enforces spending thresholds. Will escalate if cash_reserves drop below $4M.

decision_points.title: Port Closure Response
decision_points.description: The strait closure has cut your primary shipping route. You must decide how to restore cargo flow within 72 hours before inventory begins critical depletion.

options.label: Reroute through Cape of Good Hope
options.feedback: Rerouting adds 18 days and $1.5M in fuel and port fees but restores cargo flow. Inventory will draw down during the delay. Geopolitical exposure reduced.

options.label: Wait for strait reopening
options.feedback: Waiting preserves cash but inventory has dropped to 48%. Customer satisfaction is eroding. Diplomatic resolution is uncertain — geopolitical risk remains elevated.

options.label: Air freight for critical cargo
options.feedback: Air freight bridges the critical gap in 3 days but costs $2.8M. Cash reserves are now stressed. Sustainable only for 1–2 rounds before financial limits force a change.

options.label: Engage government diplomatic channel
options.feedback: Diplomatic engagement has reduced geopolitical risk by one level. Shipping delay is still 12 days during negotiations. Inventory continues to decline but the long-term outlook improves.

decision_points.title: Supplier Diversification Decision
decision_points.description: Your single-source supplier is now unable to guarantee delivery. Do you activate backup suppliers at cost, or maintain the primary relationship and accept the risk?

options.label: Activate regional backup supplier
options.feedback: Backup supplier is activated at a $1.4M setup cost. Inventory stabilises. Quality is 15% lower than primary but sufficient for continued operations. Disruption risk significantly reduced.

options.label: Maintain single supplier and renegotiate terms
options.feedback: Renegotiation is ongoing but the primary supplier is unable to deliver through the blocked route. Inventory has dropped to 42%. Customer satisfaction is declining sharply.

options.label: Emergency multi-source procurement
options.feedback: Multi-source procurement is expensive ($2.9M) but creates resilient supply architecture. Inventory recovers to 70%. Long-term exposure to single-route disruption is eliminated.

options.label: Enforce insurance performance bond
options.feedback: Insurance bond claim partially accepted. $1M recovery reduces cash pressure. Inventory continues declining but financial runway is extended. Enhanced coverage now active for rerouting premiums.

decision_points.title: Fuel Cost Management
decision_points.description: Fuel costs are now 45–120% above baseline. This is unsustainable over multiple rounds. How do you manage the fuel cost exposure?

options.label: Lock in current rates via fuel futures contract
options.feedback: Futures contract locks fuel at 155 index for 60 days at a $500K premium. Protected from further spikes. If rates fall, you overpay — but downside is capped.

options.label: Pass fuel surcharge to customers
options.feedback: Surcharge preserves margins but customer satisfaction drops to 50 and demand eases. 2 key accounts have flagged intent to seek alternative suppliers.

options.label: Absorb fuel costs from cash reserves
options.feedback: Absorbing costs protects customer relationships (satisfaction at 80) but burns $1.7M from reserves. Cash runway is now constrained to approximately 2 further rounds at this burn rate.

decision_points.title: Crisis Escalation Response
decision_points.description: The supply chain is in critical state. Inventory and cash are both stressed. An emergency decision is required to prevent operational failure.

options.label: Request government emergency logistics intervention
options.feedback: Government intervention has partially opened the strait to humanitarian and critical commercial traffic. Port capacity is at 65%. Geopolitical risk reduced to level 2. Inventory stabilising.

options.label: Charter vessels from competitor operator
options.feedback: Chartered competitor vessels at premium cost ($1.5M). Delivery restored within 5 days. Cash is significantly reduced but operations can continue.

options.label: Accept partial delivery schedule and ration supply
options.feedback: Rationing supply preserves cash but further damages customer relationships. Satisfaction drops to 40. Two major accounts have formally complained. Some demand has permanently shifted to competitors.

decision_points.title: Emergency Inventory Management
decision_points.description: Inventory levels have dropped below the critical 50% threshold. Immediate action is required to prevent operational shutdown.

options.label: Ration supply to key strategic customers only
options.feedback: Rationing protects your 5 highest-value accounts but secondary customers have begun defecting. Short-term cash position is preserved.

options.label: Emergency spot-market procurement at premium
options.feedback: Spot-market procurement at 40% premium restores inventory to 68%. Expensive ($2.2M) but prevents immediate operational crisis.

options.label: Halt non-critical operations to extend inventory runway
options.feedback: Halting non-critical lines extends inventory runway by 3 weeks but customer satisfaction has collapsed. Significant revenue loss expected.

event.title: Extreme Fuel Price Spike
event.description: Fuel prices have exceeded 190% of baseline. An automatic $400K additional cost is incurred this round.

event.title: Secondary Sanctions Risk Warning
event.description: Legal counsel advises that some alternate suppliers may trigger secondary sanctions exposure. Insurance underwriter has flagged the policy.

event.title: Critical Inventory Shortage Alert
event.description: Internal systems have triggered a Tier 1 shortage alert. All non-essential procurement suspended. Finance committee notified.

event.title: Cascading Supply Chain Failure
event.description: Extended shipping delays have triggered cascading failures in downstream production. Subcontractors are requesting force majeure provisions.

event.title: Financial Distress Warning
event.description: Cash reserves have dropped below $6M. The financial controller has escalated to the CFO. Credit facility review initiated.

outcome_conditions.description: Supply chain has completely collapsed. Operations suspended. Emergency board meeting convened. Regulatory and contractual penalties triggered.
Cash reserves have dropped below $3M. Immediate access to credit facilities required. Operations under severe financial stress.
Customer satisfaction has collapsed below 30. Formal contract termination notices received from three major accounts.
Supply chain has stabilised. Inventory is at 70%+ with minimal shipping delays. Normal operations are resuming.
Full operational recovery achieved. Inventory restored, financials healthy, and supply chain architecture strengthened.
